 Home » Nation Vote Counting Underway In Rajasthan Rural Body Elections
 Nation PTI 20 Nov 2026 9:09 AM IST 20 Nov 2026 9:09 AM IST Members of several prominent political families are also in the fray.
 x As Preferred
Source Jaipur: Counting of votes for the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections began in 37 districts of Rajasthan at 8 am on Friday to decide the fate of more than 29,000 candidates.The results are significant for the ruling BJP and the opposition Congress as both seek control of rural local bodies across the state.
 Members of several prominent political families are also in the fray.
 In Churu, former BJP MLA Rajendra Rathore's son Parakram Singh and daughter-in-law Kanika Singh are contesting Zila Parishad elections, along with Kanak Budania, wife of Congress MLA Narendra Budania.
 Urban Development and Housing minister Jhabar Singh Kharra's wife Shanti Devi and sons Ajay Singh and Durga Singh are contesting elections in Shrimadhopur panchayat samiti in Sikar.
 Other prominent candidates include Nikita Dudi, daughter-in-law of former Congress MP Rameshwar Dudi, in Bikaner; Amin Khan Fakir and Amardin Fakir, brothers of former Congress MLA and minister Saleh Mohammad, in Jaisalmer and Beena Bairwa, wife of Congress MLA D C Bairwa, in Dausa.
 According to the state election commission, 4,069 candidates contested 1,275 Zila Parishad wards, while 25,108 candidates were in the fray for 7,543 Panchayat Samiti wards across 419 Panchayat Samitis in 37 districts where counting is being held today.
 More than 2.48 crore votes were polled at 41,480 polling stations during the four-phase elections held on October 22, October 28, November 3 and November 14.
 Counting is being held in all districts except Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar, where the exercise has been deferred to December 17 as the five-year terms of the existing Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis expire in December.
 These four districts have 128 Zila Parishad wards and 702 Panchayat Samiti wards spread across 38 Panchayat Samitis. A total of 3,227 candidates contested the elections in these districts, where more than 24.51 lakh votes were polled.
 Across all 41 districts, the elections covered 1,403 Zila Parishad wards and 8,245 Panchayat Samiti wards in 457 Panchayat Samitis. A total of 32,404 candidates contested the elections, and more than 2.73 crore votes were polled at 45,385 polling stations.
 In the previous Panchayati Raj elections held during 2020-21, the BJP won 1,989 Panchayat Samiti seats against the Congress's 1,852 in 21 districts in December 2020. The Congress subsequently won 678 seats against the BJP's 551 in six districts in September 2021, and 278 against 165 in four districts in December 2021.
 The number of Zila Parishad seats has since increased from 1,014 to 1,403 and Panchayat Samiti seats from 6,992 to 8,245.
 The newly elected Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members will subsequently elect the heads of their respective bodies.
 Elections for Zila Pramukhs are scheduled for November 25, followed by Up-Zila Pramukhs on November 26. Panchayat Samiti Pradhans will be elected on November 27 and Up-Pradhans on November 28.
 In the four districts where counting has been deferred, elections for Zila Pramukhs and Up-Zila Pramukhs will be held on December 22 and 23, respectively, while Pradhans and Up-Pradhans will be elected on December 24 and 25.
